title: SC-500
subtitle: Microsoft SC-500 · end-to-end security controls for cloud and AI workloads
releaseNote: beta.1 — 17 games across the April-2026 outline. No quiz: the sim commits capital before it asks anything, and every board is a sort, not a stem.
studyContext: I am studying for the Microsoft SC-500 exam, Implementing End-to-End Security Controls for Cloud and AI Workloads (outline effective 2026-04-26).
citeInstruction: Cite the SC-500 exam outline domain and area (for example "Area 3.1 — implement security for AI") and, where relevant, the Microsoft Learn documentation page the control is described on.

groups.label: Watch Floor
groups.blurb: The flagship simulation — the whole outline played under pressure instead of quizzed.

games.title: The Watch Floor
games.blurb: Fifteen turns, twelve desks, never enough budget. Spend to hold a desk before you know what it will ask, and contain what gets through.

games.title: Who Gets In
games.blurb: Sort access scenes to the Entra control that actually solves them — PIM, Conditional Access, an authentication method, or a workload identity.

games.title: One Condition Apart
games.blurb: Two policies, one variable flipped, two very different blast radii. Tell them apart before a tenant does it for you.

games.title: Chain of Custody
games.blurb: Keys, secrets, certificates and the managed identities that reach them — sort each scene to the custody control it needs.

games.title: Make It Stick
games.blurb: A rule nobody enforces is a suggestion. Sort each governance need to the mechanism that makes it binding.

games.title: Left Open
games.blurb: Every storage account leaks a different way. Sort the exposure to the control that closes it.

games.title: Near Misses
games.blurb: Database controls that sound interchangeable and are not — one variable apart, two different outcomes.

games.title: Hold the Edge
games.blurb: Firewall, WAF, DDoS, private link, NSG. Sort each traffic problem to the service that is actually built for it.

games.title: Blast Radius
games.blurb: Agents have identities now, and identities have reach. Sort each AI exposure to the surface that governs it.

games.title: Guardrail or Gate
games.blurb: Foundry guardrails, AI Gateway policies and Defender for AI overlap in the brochure and not in the portal.

games.title: Harden the Host
games.blurb: Sort each server and VM weakness to the control that removes it rather than the one that merely reports it.

games.title: Platform Rules
games.blurb: Containers, App Service, Functions and AKS each fail differently. Sort the scene to the platform control that fits.

games.title: Score and Sort
games.blurb: Defender for Cloud tells you everything at once. Sort each finding to what it actually is — recommendation, attack path, alert, or governance rule.

games.title: Get the Signal In
games.blurb: Connectors, collection rules, normalization and retention — sort each ingestion problem to the Sentinel mechanism that solves it.

games.title: Two Tables Apart
games.blurb: Analytics rule or hunting query, table or basic log, UEBA or anomaly. Flip one variable and the cost changes with the answer.

games.title: Ask It Properly
games.blurb: Plugins, promptbooks, compute units and the embedded experiences — sort each need to the Security Copilot surface that serves it.

games.title: In Order
games.blurb: Reconstruct the response sequences — onboarding a connector, running down an incident, tuning a noisy rule. Unscored practice.
